problem_statement:
Accept binary bytes on the PDF header line
I have a pdf  [vittel_rdc.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26108134/vittel_rdc.pdf) that fails to load in lopdf with
```
Error: Parse(invalid file header)
```
but otherwise opens fine in other pdf viewers.

After some investigations it looks like it has a header with something like
```
%PDF-1.3 \xb0\x9f\x92\x9c\x9f\xd4\xe0\xce\xd0\xd0\xd0\r
```
and was produced by ImageMill Imaging Library v3.000.

If I understand correctly, the pdf spec (ISO 32000, §7.5.2) would requires a newline before the binary comment line and that's what lopdf implements. However looking at what other pdf libraries implement they are a bit less strict,

- **pypdf**: Only validates the 5-byte `%PDF-` prefix, doesn't parse the rest of the line
- **pdf.js** (Mozilla): Reads version chars until whitespace (byte ≤ 0x20) or 7 chars max, ignores the rest
- **qpdf**: Uses regex `[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` to extract version digits, ignores trailing bytes

so I would propose to be a bit less strict about this header parsing, to not error on such files. There should be little downside.

Made a PR in https://github.com/J-F-Liu/lopdf/pull/481
all_hints_text:
pypdf can set a parameter: strict=False/True, lopdf should also support this.
Thanks for the feedback! I'll add it to the PR. 

Do you want the default to be strict=true or false? In pypdf it looks like they switched the default from true to false eventually. 
And also API wise @J-F-Liu if I try to add a strict flag in #481. Would you prefer,
```rs
  let doc = Document::load_with_options("file.pdf", &LoadOptions::lenient())?;
  let doc = Document::load_mem_with_options(&bytes, &LoadOptions::lenient())?;
```
or 
```rs
Document::load_lenient("f.pdf")?;
// load remains the strict version
```

or some other pattern?

> Do you want the default to be strict=true or false?

I imagine strict by default for backward compatibility?
I suggest keep `Document::load`, add `Document::load_with_options` to replace `load_with_password` and `load_filtered`.
Default to strict=false is ok.
rebuild_cmds: cd /testbed && cargo build ; cargo build --manifest-path pdfutil/Cargo.toml
test_cmds: cd /testbed && mkdir -p reports && cargo test --verbose -- --test-threads=1 2>&1 | tee reports/test-output.log
log_parser:
def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import re

    def strip_ansi(s: str) -> str:
        return re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]", "", s)

    log = "\n".join(strip_ansi(l) for l in log.splitlines())

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    current_suite = None

    # Rust/cargo suite identification
    run_re = re.compile(r"^\s*Running\s+`.*?/deps/([^/\s`]+?)(?:-[0-9a-f]{8,})?(?:\s|`|$)")
    # Rust libtest per-test line
    rust_test_re = re.compile(r"^\s*test\s+(.+?)\s+\.\.\.\s+(ok|FAILED|ignored)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    # Rust failure header: ---- testname stdout ----
    rust_fail_hdr_re = re.compile(r"^\s*----\s+(.+?)\s+stdout\s+----\s*$")
    # Rust failures list section
    rust_fail_list_start = re.compile(r"^\s*failures:\s*$")
    rust_fail_item = re.compile(r"^\s{4}(.+?)\s*$")

    # Other frameworks (best-effort)
    go_re = re.compile(r"^\s*---\s+(PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(\S+)", re.IGNORECASE)
    pytest_re = re.compile(r"^\s*([^:\s]+::\S+)\s+(PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|XFAIL|XPASS|ERROR)\b")
    unittest_re = re.compile(r"^\s*(\S+)\s+\.\.\.\s+(ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    jest_re = re.compile(r"^\s*(PASS|FAIL)\s+(\S+)")

    # JUnit XML (very rough streaming parse)
    testcase_open_re = re.compile(r"<testcase\b[^>]*\bname=\"([^\"]+)\"[^>]*>", re.IGNORECASE)
    testcase_close_re = re.compile(r"</testcase>", re.IGNORECASE)
    failure_re = re.compile(r"<(failure|error)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    skipped_re = re.compile(r"<skipped\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    in_testcase = False
    tc_name = None
    tc_fail = False
    tc_skip = False

    in_failures_section = False

    def qualify(name: str) -> str:
        name = name.strip()
        if current_suite:
            return f"{current_suite}::{name}"
        return name

    for line in log.splitlines():
        # update suite
        m = run_re.match(line)
        if m:
            current_suite = m.group(1)
            in_failures_section = False
            continue

        # rust per-test
        m = rust_test_re.match(line)
        if m:
            name = qualify(m.group(1))
            status = m.group(2).lower()
            if status == "ok":
                results[name] = "pass"
            elif status == "ignored":
                results[name] = "skip"
            else:
                results[name] = "fail"
            in_failures_section = False
            continue

        # rust failure header
        m = rust_fail_hdr_re.match(line)
        if m:
            results[qualify(m.group(1))] = "fail"
            in_failures_section = False
            continue

        # rust failures list
        if rust_fail_list_start.match(line):
            in_failures_section = True
            continue
        if in_failures_section:
            m = rust_fail_item.match(line)
            if m:
                item = m.group(1).strip()
                if item:
                    results[qualify(item)] = "fail"
                continue
            else:
                in_failures_section = False

        # Go
        m = go_re.match(line)
        if m:
            st = m.group(1).lower()
            name = qualify(m.group(2))
            results[name] = "pass" if st == "pass" else "skip" if st == "skip" else "fail"
            continue

        # pytest
        m = pytest_re.match(line)
        if m:
            name = qualify(m.group(1))
            st = m.group(2).upper()
            if st in ("PASSED", "XPASS"):
                results[name] = "pass"
            elif st in ("SKIPPED", "XFAIL"):
                results[name] = "skip"
            else:
                results[name] = "fail"
            continue

        # unittest
        m = unittest_re.match(line)
        if m:
            name = qualify(m.group(1))
            st = m.group(2).lower()
            if st == "ok":
                results[name] = "pass"
            elif st == "skipped":
                results[name] = "skip"
            else:
                results[name] = "fail"
            continue

        # jest
        m = jest_re.match(line)
        if m:
            results[qualify(m.group(2))] = "pass" if m.group(1).upper() == "PASS" else "fail"
            continue

        # JUnit XML
        if not in_testcase:
            m = testcase_open_re.search(line)
            if m:
                in_testcase = True
                tc_name = qualify(m.group(1))
                tc_fail = bool(failure_re.search(line))
                tc_skip = bool(skipped_re.search(line))
                if testcase_close_re.search(line):
                    results[tc_name] = "fail" if tc_fail else "skip" if tc_skip else "pass"
                    in_testcase = False
                    tc_name = None
            continue
        else:
            if failure_re.search(line):
                tc_fail = True
            if skipped_re.search(line):
                tc_skip = True
            if testcase_close_re.search(line):
                results[tc_name] = "fail" if tc_fail else "skip" if tc_skip else "pass"
                in_testcase = False
                tc_name = None
            continue

    return results
